Injected an invalid document reference ('ghost-doc-xyz') into both a document's relatedDocs array and a content section's links array via direct mutation of the live in-memory documents module (same singleton used by the running React app), then forced re-render by re-navigating to the document. In both code paths, the app's render logic resolves each reference via a document lookup and silently omits any entry that doesn't resolve to a real document. Section 'REST Principles' data had 3 links (including the injected ghost one) but the rendered UI only showed 2 clickable link buttons (API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards) — the invalid 'Ghost Document' link never appeared in the DOM at all. Same result for Related Documents panel. Since no broken/invalid link is ever rendered as clickable, the user can never trigger a broken navigation — the app fully prevents the error condition rather than merely catching it post-click.
